doc.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023

chapter: Performing and the idea of free jazz
title: There is no such thing as free jazz; Ornette Coleman
summary: He rejects the term free jazz as a critics' label and praises Ornette Coleman's 1961 record and the musicians on it as the work of stellar musicians.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Are the expectations in — I wish there was a better term than free jazz. Maybe you have one.
There is no such thing as free jazz.
There is no such thing as free jazz.
Because not hard as I’m working. You know. There’s no such thing as free jazz. You know that’s just something that critics came up with you know.
Do you think that Ornette Coleman’s LP back in ’61 was an unfortunate —
It was a monster. It was a monster. Ornette Coleman’s record is a monster you know, him and Don Cherry and Charlie Haden, Ed Blackwell. That is some stellar music.
But did he call it free jazz do you know?

Well I don’t know, I don’t know what he called it but I mean it’s not free jazz. You get up there and do what Ornette Coleman did. That ain’t no free jazz man. You know. And there was piece —all of these pieces you know, like that, that beautiful ballad that Ornette wrote you know. Ornette was a stellar musician you know.
And he paid a lot of dues for what he did.

I don’t think that he did. I mean like in the end he triumphed and won. You know everybody knew like you know you don’t become Ornette Coleman by not knowing what you’re doing. You know you don’t do that.
